title: Recurring individual leakers
disclaimer: Archive-based reliability signal, not a guarantee. A person can be accurate on one claim and wrong on another; repeated coverage of the same post is not independent confirmation.

leakers.name: Steve Hemmerstoffer
leakers.note: Appears repeatedly behind early S22, S23, S25 and S27 design renders. The archive treats CAD as useful shape evidence, not a final production blueprint. His S27 and S27 Ultra CAD sets currently disagree with Ice Universe about the Ultra's rear camera treatment, so neither reading is treated as settled.

references.title: S27 and S27 Ultra CAD renders

leakers.name: Ice Universe
leakers.note: Frequently attributed across the S22, S23 Ultra and S27 records for camera, display, battery and chipset claims. In August 2026 the account posted a camera-plateau sketch and case images for the S27 Pro and Ultra that conflict with the OnLeaks CAD camera bar; the archive preserves both and treats neither as confirmed. Individual claims still need separate verification.

references.title: S23 Ultra camera and display reports
S27 CAD speaker and magnet details

leakers.name: Evan Blass
leakers.note: The S25 archive records additional renders attributed to him, making him a notable source for official-looking pre-launch imagery rather than a general specification oracle.

leakers.name: Yogesh Brar
leakers.note: Named in S23 reporting for camera and chipset specifications. The archive keeps his claims distinct from later launch confirmation.

leakers.name: Ross Young
leakers.note: The S23 archive cites him for an early limited-color prediction. This is a narrower signal than a complete device specification leak.

leakers.name: Robin Quandt
leakers.note: The S23 archive attributes apparent Snapdragon marketing and comparison material to him. Material provenance matters more than the outlet repeating it.

leakers.name: Tron
leakers.note: Named by Notebookcheck in the early S22 Exynos/AMD and Snapdragon regional specification trail. The archive records the regional uncertainty rather than treating it as certainty.

leakers.name: Jukanlosreve
leakers.note: The S25 record attributes leaked S25+ hands-on images to this account, including the camera rings and US mmWave antenna.

leakers.name: Sonny Dickson
leakers.note: The S27 record attributes a wide camera-plateau image report to him. The archive treats image interpretation, such as possible Qi2 magnets, as unconfirmed.

leakers.name: Anthony
leakers.note: The S27 record attributes several early camera, display and chipset claims to this account, but the underlying posts were not independently preserved; it is listed for traceability, not endorsement.

references.title: S27 Ultra camera and display claims

leakers.name: Setsuna Digital
leakers.note: Credited by Gizmochina for the earliest S27 S Pen-slot rumor currently located in the archive. One early report is not enough to establish a reliability record.

leakers.name: kro
leakers.note: On 2 September 2026 posted Galaxy S27 Edge figures — a 5.8-inch display, a low-4 mm body and a 4,300 mAh battery — without stating a source, and a second X account contradicted the size the same day. A single uncorroborated post is not a reliability record, so the archive lists the account for traceability only.

references.title: S27 Edge size and battery claim
Edge rumor context and silicon-carbon relay

leakers.name: SPYGO19726
leakers.note: Replied to the S27 Edge post on 2 September 2026 with a different size — 6.8 inches at 5.4 mm — and no stated source, without disputing the battery figure. The archive has one appearance for this account and treats it as unproven.

leakers.name: Lanzuk
leakers.handle: tipster account (handle not stated in the reporting)
leakers.note: A July 2026 report attributed to this account said silicon-carbon batteries would reach the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra at roughly 10% more capacity than their S26 equivalents, that the base model was undecided on cost and that the chemistry currently degrades faster than lithium-ion. The archive located the claim only through a secondary relay and has not read the original post.

leakers.name: Abhishek Yadav
leakers.handle: tipster account (handle not stated in the reporting)
leakers.note: Relayed the China 3C registry listing behind the reported 25 W and 45 W Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus charging speeds. The firmer evidence is the regulatory listing rather than the relay, and this archive did not inspect the registry entry itself.
